subject: Chemistry
title: Nucleophilic Substitution in Haloarenes: S_NAr & Benzyne Pathways
topics: 4.1 S_NAr Addition-Elimination Mechanism in Activated Haloarenes
Meisenheimer Intermediate (Carbanion σ-complex) Resonance Stabilization by o,p-Nitro Groups
Activation Trajectory for Chlorobenzene (Dow Process 623 K/300 atm ──► o-Nitro 443 K ──► 2,4-Dinitro 368 K ──► Picryl Chloride Warm H₂O)
Why Meta-Nitro Groups Do NOT Activate S_NAr (Negative charge never resides on meta carbon)
4.2 Elimination-Addition Mechanism via Benzyne Intermediate (NaNH₂ / liq. NH₃ at -33°C, Cine Substitution)
quickSummary: Haloarenes undergo substitution via: 1. S_NAr (Addition-Elimination) when activated by o,p-nitro groups stabilizing the Meisenheimer carbanion intermediate. Dow process requires 623 K/300 atm, but picryl chloride reacts with warm water alone. Meta-nitro groups do not activate. 2. Benzyne pathway (Elimination-Addition) using NaNH₂/liq. NH₃ at -33°C via strained benzyne intermediate (lateral sp²-sp² overlap in ring plane), yielding cine substitution.
summary: Master S_NAr addition-elimination with Meisenheimer complexes and the benzyne elimination-addition pathway.

summaryBox.title: S_NAr Activation Trajectory
summaryBox.takeaway: o,p-NO₂ groups delocalize negative charge into oxygens via -M resonance. Picryl chloride (2,4,6-trinitro) hydrolyzes in warm water alone to Picric Acid!

$S_N\text{Ar}$ MEISENHEIMER COMPLEX STABILIZATION
                    
          Cl  OH                Cl  OH                Cl  OH
          │ /                   │ /                   │ /
          
         /   \     ────────►   / \⁻    ────────►     /   \
        |     |               |   |                 |     |
         \___/                 \ /                   \___/
           │                    │                      │
           N⁺                   N⁺                     N⁺
         // \                 // \                   // \

                   ACTIVATION TRAJECTORY FOR CHLOROBENZENE
                   
   Chlorobenzene ───────────────────────────────► $\text{NaOH, } 623\text{ K, } 300\text{ atm}$ (Dow Process) ──► Phenol
   *o*-Nitrochlorobenzene ──────────────────────► $\text{NaOH, } 443\text{ K}$ ──────────────────────► *o*-Nitrophenol
   2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene ──────────────────► $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{/H}_2\text{O, } 368\text{ K}$ ──────────────► 2,4-Dinitrophenol
   2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (Picryl Chloride)► **Warm }\text{H}_2\text{O alone!** ────────────────────► **Picric Acid**
conceptBreakdown.content:
In $S_N\text{Ar}$, strong electron-withdrawing groups ($-\text{NO}_2$) at *ortho* and *para* positions stabilize the negatively charged Meisenheimer Carbanion $\sigma$-complex.
- **Why Meta-Nitro Does Not Activate**: The negative charge in the Meisenheimer intermediate never lands on the carbon bearing the $-\text{NO}_2$ group, losing $-M$ resonance stabilization.

conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Benzyne Elimination-Addition Mechanism
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BENZYNE ELIMINATION-ADDITION
                        
   Chlorobenzene ──[$\text{NaNH}_2/\text{liq. NH}_3$]──► **BENZYNE INTERMEDIATE** ──[$\text{NH}_3$ Addition]──► Aniline
   (Elimination of $\text{HCl}$)                        (Contains a formal $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ bond)   (Cine Substitution)

                     BENZYNE TRIPLE BOND STRUCTURE
                     
   The formal triple bond in Benzyne is formed by the lateral overlap of two **$sp^2$ hybridized orbitals**
   lying in the plane of the ring, outside the aromatic $\pi$-system. It is highly strained and reactive!
conceptBreakdown.content: Unactivated haloarenes react with ultra-strong bases ($\text{NaNH}_2 / \text{liquid NH}_3$ at $-33^\circ\text{C}$) via a Benzyne Intermediate, leading to cine substitution.

quickRevision: S_NAr proceeds via a negatively charged Meisenheimer carbanion complex.
o,p-NO₂ groups accelerate S_NAr via -M resonance stabilization.
Picryl chloride converts to Picric Acid with warm water alone.
Meta-NO₂ groups do not stabilize the Meisenheimer carbanion.
Benzyne intermediate forms by elimination with NaNH₂/liq. NH₃ (sp²-sp² lateral triple bond).
